newsitem.title: USA: "Toy Story II" sequel heads straight to video.
newsitem.headline: "Toy Story II" sequel heads straight to video.

text.p: Walt Disney Co and Pixar Animation Studios on Wednesday said they will release a sequel to the highly successful computer animated movie "Toy Story" straight to home video markets

The release bypasses movie theaters, but helps speed production time by utilizing the same technology. The strategy was used for sequels like "Aladdin and the King of Thieves" and "Honey We Shrunk Ourselves".
"We are able to work with many of the same computer models of characters, sets and props as in the original film," said Ralph Guggenheim, producer of the sequel, "Toy Story II".
"This enables us to create the new movie in less time, while maintaining the same quality and sophisticated animation and story," Guggenheim added.
Released in October 1995, "Toy Story" grossed more than $350 million in global box office receipts before becoming 1996's top-selling home video, Disney said in a statement.

Tom Hanks and Tim Allen, who were the voice for the original movie's two main characters, will reprise their roles in the sequel. Hanks played "Woody" the cowboy and Allen "Buzz Lightyear" the space ranger.
